newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks federal support for more mammograms.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks federal support for more mammograms.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he wanted to ensure the Medicare and Medicaid insurance programmes and federal employee health plans support a new recommendation that women in their 40s get mammograms.

"Today I am taking action to bring Medicare, Medicaid and the federal employee health plans in line with the National Cancer Institute's recommendations," Clinton said. He referred to a new recommendation by an advisory panel of the National Cancer Institute that women in their 40s at average risk for breast cancer get mammograms every year or two.
In a brief chat with reporters, Clinton said he would send Congress on Thursday a Medicare budget that would make annual mammogram screening a covered expense for women beginning at age 40.

In addition, he said Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala was urging state Medicaid directors to cover the same expense -- Medicaid is a state-run program -- and assuring them that "the federal government will pay its matching share if they do so."

Clinton said he also directed the U.S. Office of Personnel Management to require all federal health benefit plans to comply with the cancer panel's recommendations on mammogram screenings beginning next year.

He also encouraged private insurers to support the mamography guidelines. "The federal government is doing its part to make sure women have both coverage and access to this potentially life saving test," Clinton said. "I want to challenge private health insurance plans to do the same."
